t: So the number people quote is ninety percent. Ninety percent of the cases in that pilot were resolved without a hearing. And every time I put that slide up, somebody in the room writes it down.

What the slide does not say is which cases went into the pilot. They were the ones both sides had already agreed to send there. So what the ninety percent measures is not whether the system works. It measures whether people who have already agreed can be brought to sign something.
I am not saying the pilot failed. I am saying we have a number that answers a different question from the one we asked.
You said the cases were pre-selected. Does that hold for the second year as well, or was that only the first round?
Good — the second year opened it up, and the figure drops to sixty-one. Which is still worth having. It is just a different claim.
